Evidence: ABC career, AFR editor, That's Business podcast

Alan Kohler concludes an extraordinary 31-year career at the ABC, having transformed financial journalism with clarity and warmth.

Kohler's legendary career as a finance communicator leaves an enduring legacy of public trust and economic literacy across Australia.

Kohler ran a smart altruistic loop for decades, pairing transparent market analysis with genuine audience empowerment to demystify finance.

The Unavoidable Lie: Individual retirement marks the end of an institutional ethos.

It's hard to imagine the evening news without his friendly graphs and reassuring smile. Thank you for decades of making the numbers make sense.

Alan Kohler says he is ready to spend more time with his family. (Supplied: Alan Kohler)

After a brilliant 31-year career as the ABC's finance guru, Alan Kohler has decided to hang up his boots at the end of the year.

With a successful career in print before moving to television, Kohler has been one of the most influential journalists Australia has ever produced, as a former editor of The Australian Financial Review (AFR) and The Age and as an incisive columnist on all affairs financial.

"I love the ABC, always have, even more so after I joined it," he told ABC staff in a statement.

Alan Kohler (left) speaks with then-treasurer Paul Keating in 1984, during Kohler's time as editor of The Australian Financial Review.  (Supplied)

Kohler joined the public broadcaster in 1995 as business and economics correspondent for the 7.30 Report and went on to host Inside Business.

For the past 24 years, he has been the lead 7pm News finance presenter, unravelling the mysteries of financial markets for the audience with a format all his own that has often begun with: "Now, here's an interesting graph."

ABC managing director Hugh Marks said Kohler had made an extraordinary contribution to the organisation and the nation.

Alan Kohler swapped the studio for the home office during COVID-19 pandemic. (Supplied)

"For decades, he has helped Australians make sense of complex issues with insight, clarity and a uniquely engaging style, always delivered with warmth, humour and that trademark cheeky grin.

"I can't thank Alan enough for everything he has given to the ABC and our audiences. While this marks the end of an incredible chapter, it is certainly not the end of Alan's contribution, just the beginning of a new one."

Kohler hosted Inside Business for many years. He currently writes a weekly column and hosts a podcast, That's Business, every Friday.

While he is a distinguished editor, Kohler's biggest impact on the nation has been as a communicator.

After several stints as the chanticleer columnist for the AFR, he joined The Sydney Morning Herald (SMH) and The Age as senior business columnist, working with your correspondent during my time as SMH business editor.

Alan Kohler worked as a journalist in Darwin during Cyclone Tracey. (Supplied)

A canny entrepreneur, he had by that stage already launched The Eureka Report and later left Fairfax Media when he added online news service Business Spectator to the mix.

Throughout his various incarnations, he has remained steadfastly loyal to the ABC and to his audience and is expected to continue his association with one-off specials.
